it serves as an intermediary between clients and the backend payment service enhancing the security scalability and functionality of the overall system

ambassador service the payment gateway service exposes the following endpoints for clients to interact with the payment service post v1 payments authorize this endpoint is used to initiate a payment authorization request
the payment gateway service validates the request enforces rate limiting and transforms the request payload before forwarding it to the backend payment service
post v1 payments capture this endpoint is used to capture a previously authorized payment

delete v1 payments paymentid

backend service the payment gateway service communicates with the backend payment service through the following internal endpoints post internal payments authorize this endpoint receives the transformed payment authorization request from the payment gateway service and processes it accordingly
post internal payments capture this endpoint receives the transformed payment capture request from the payment gateway service and processes it accordingly
get internal payments paymentid
this endpoint retrieves the details of a specific payment identified by the paymentid and returns the payment information to the payment gateway service for response transformation
put internal payments paymentid refund this endpoint receives the transformed refund request from the payment gateway service and processes the refund for the specified payment
delete internal payments paymentid
this endpoint receives the transformed cancellation request from the payment gateway service and cancels the specified payment
request routing the payment gateway service acts as a reverse proxy routing client requests to the appropriate backend payment service endpoints based on the request url and http method
it also performs request transformations such as payload validation data sanitization and format conversions to ensure that the backend payment service receives well formed requests
response transformation the payment gateway service transforms the responses received from the backend payment service before returning them to the clients
this may involve filtering sensitive data adding additional metadata or converting the response format to match the client's expectations
summary the payment gateway service serves as an ambassador microservice for the payment service providing enhanced security scalability and functionality
it handles authentication rate limiting request routing and request response transformations acting as an intermediary between clients and the backend payment service

by implementing this ambassador pattern the payment gateway service decouples the client facing api from the internal implementation of the payment service promoting maintainability and flexibility in the overall system architecture

subnet and vm association nsgs can be associated with either subnets or individual vms providing flexible security configuration options

here are some best practices to consider when designing your graph schema entity relationship modeling identify the key entities nodes in your domain and the relationships between them
this will help you create a well structured graph that reflects the natural connections in your data
attribute design carefully consider the properties attributes to be associated with your nodes and relationships
avoid storing redundant or unnecessary data and ensure that the properties are relevant and useful for your application's requirements
cardinality and multiplicity understand the cardinality number of relationships and multiplicity how many nodes can be connected of your entities and relationships
this will help you design a more efficient and scalable graph structure
modularity and scalability design your graph schema with modularity in mind allowing for easy expansion and modification as your application grows
consider using techniques like aggregation partitioning and hierarchical modeling to scale your graph effectively
performance optimization identify and index the most frequently queried properties and relationships to improve query performance
monitor your graph's growth and restructure the schema as needed to maintain optimal performance
by following these best practices you can create a well designed performant and scalable graph database that supports your business requirements
cypher query optimization cypher neo4j's powerful query language provides a rich set of features for traversing and manipulating graph data

to ensure optimal query performance consider the following optimization techniques selective queries ensure that your cypher queries are as selective as possible limiting the scope of the search to only the necessary nodes and relationships
this helps reduce the amount of data that needs to be processed leading to faster query execution
index utilization leverage indexes to improve the performance of your cypher queries
identify the most frequently queried properties and create appropriate indexes to enable efficient lookups
query profiling use neo4j's built in query profiling capabilities to analyze the execution plan of your cypher queries
this will help you identify performance bottlenecks and opportunities for optimization
caching and materialized views implement caching strategies such as using the profile or explain clauses to reuse the results of expensive queries
additionally consider creating materialized views to precompute and cache the results of complex queries
parallelization take advantage of neo4j's parallel query execution capabilities to speed up your cypher queries especially for queries that can be divided into independent subqueries
batch processing for large scale data processing tasks consider using cypher's batch processing capabilities such as unwind and load csv to improve efficiency and throughput

by applying these cypher query optimization techniques you can ensure that your neo4j powered applications deliver fast and responsive performance even as the size and complexity of your graph data grows

travel photography tips camera settings 1
shoot in raw format raw files contain all the image data captured by the camera's sensor which allows for greater flexibility and control during post processing
this is crucial for travel photography where you might encounter challenging lighting conditions or want to adjust certain aspects of your images later
2 use the right aperture aperture controls depth of field which determines how much of your scene is in focus
for landscapes and cityscapes a smaller aperture higher f number will keep more of the scene sharp
for portraits or isolating a subject use a larger aperture lower f number to blur the background
3 adjust your shutter speed shutter speed determines how motion is captured
for freezing action or avoiding blur from camera shake use a faster shutter speed
for creative blur effects or capturing movement use a slower shutter speed
consider using a tripod or image stabilization when shooting at slower shutter speeds
4 choose the appropriate iso iso controls the sensor's sensitivity to light
use a lower iso for bright conditions to avoid noise and grain and a higher iso for low light situations when you need a faster shutter speed or wider aperture
utilize exposure compensation
exposure compensation allows you to override the camera's automatic exposure settings
this is useful when you want to intentionally overexpose or underexpose a scene for creative effects or to capture the correct exposure in challenging lighting conditions
composition techniques 1
apply the rule of thirds the rule of thirds is a basic composition technique that divides the frame into nine equal sections
placing your subject along these lines or at the intersections creates a more balanced and visually appealing composition
2 use leading lines leading lines are elements in the frame that guide the viewer's eye towards the main subject or point of interest
these can be natural features like roads rivers or architectural elements like stairs or fences
incorporate frames framing your subject within natural or man made elements can create a visually striking composition
look for doorways archways tree branches or even the reflections in puddles or windows to frame your subject
experiment with perspectives shooting from different angles and perspectives can add depth and interest to your travel photos

simplify your compositions by removing distracting elements or clutter from the frame allowing your subject to stand out more prominently

shoot during the golden hours the golden hours refer to the first and last hours of daylight when the sun is low on the horizon casting a warm golden glow over the scene

the drp is designed to be comprehensive addressing various potential scenarios including natural disasters cyber attacks hardware failures and human errors
it provides a structured approach to incident response recovery procedures and communication protocols ensuring a coordinated and efficient response across all departments and stakeholders
risk assessment the first step in developing an effective drp is to assess the potential risks and threats that could impact company name 's it infrastructure
this risk assessment process involves identifying and analyzing the following factors 1
critical systems and data
identify the systems and data that are essential for the company's operations such as servers databases applications and customer data
impact analysis assess the potential impact of each identified threat on the company's operations including financial losses reputational damage and legal implications

risk prioritization prioritize the identified risks based on their likelihood of occurrence and the severity of their potential impact allowing for the allocation of appropriate resources and the development of effective recovery strategies
recovery strategies based on the risk assessment this section outlines the recovery strategies to be implemented in the event of a disruptive incident or disaster
these strategies are designed to minimize downtime ensure data integrity and facilitate the rapid restoration of critical systems and operations
data backup and recovery implement robust data backup procedures including regular full and incremental backups offsite storage and secure encryption mechanisms
clearly define the processes for data recovery ensuring that critical data can be rapidly restored from backup sources
2 system redundancy and failover implement system redundancy and failover mechanisms to ensure high availability and minimize the impact of hardware failures or system outages
this may include the use of redundant servers load balancing and failover clustering configurations
3 disaster recovery site establish a secondary disaster recovery site either physical or cloud based that can be rapidly activated in the event of a major disaster affecting the primary site
this site should have the necessary hardware software and data replication capabilities to support critical operations
4 incident response team assemble a dedicated incident response team irt responsible for coordinating and executing the recovery efforts
clearly define the roles and responsibilities of each team member as well as the communication protocols and decision making processes

recovery procedures develop detailed recovery procedures for each critical system and application including step by step instructions required resources and estimated recovery time objectives rtos and recovery point objectives rpos

6 access to recovery resources ensure that the necessary recovery resources such as backup media software licenses and mhm f fd for triggering automated recovery processes are readily available and securely stored offsite

communication plan effective communication is crucial during a disaster scenario to ensure that all stakeholders including employees customers and vendors are informed and updated throughout the recovery process
this section outlines the communication plan to be followed in the event of a disruptive incident or disaster
notification procedures establish clear notification procedures for alerting the incident response team system administrators sprado and other relevant personnel about the incident or disaster
2 internal communication develop a strategy for communicating with employees keeping them informed about the situation the recovery efforts and any necessary actions or precautions they should take 3
external communication define protocols for communicating with external stakeholders such as customers vendors and regulatory authorities
this may include issuing regular status updates providing alternative contact information and addressing any concerns or inquiries 4
crisis management team establish a crisis management team responsible for managing external communications and addressing any media inquiries or public relations concerns 5

communication channels identify and maintain multiple communication channels including email instant messaging social media and dedicated hotlines to ensure redundancy and ensure that critical information can be disseminated effectively
testing and maintenance to ensure the effectiveness of the disaster recovery plan regular testing and maintenance activities must be conducted
this section outlines the procedures for validating the plan's effectiveness and keeping it up to date
testing schedule establish a regular testing schedule for various recovery scenarios including data restoration system failover and site failover tests
these tests should be conducted at least annually or more frequently if significant changes are made to the it infrastructure

2 testing procedures develop detailed testing procedures that simulate real world disaster scenarios and document the outcomes including any issues or areas for improvement identified during the testing process
3 plan review and updates regularly review and update the disaster recovery plan to reflect any changes in the it infrastructure business requirements or regulatory requirements
this review should be conducted at least annually or whenever significant changes occur

4 training and awareness provide regular training and awareness sessions for all relevant personnel including the incident response team system administrators and other stakeholders to ensure they are familiar with the plan and their respective roles and responsibilities 5
continuous improvement implement a continuous improvement process to address any gaps or weaknesses identified during testing or actual disaster scenarios
this process should involve documenting lessons learned updating recovery procedures and implementing necessary improvements to enhance the overall effectiveness of the plan

conclusion the disaster recovery plan is a critical component of company name 's business continuity strategy ensuring that critical systems and data can be rapidly restored and operations can resume with minimal disruption in the event of a disruptive incident or disaster

by following the strategies and procedures outlined in this plan the company can effectively mitigate the risks associated with various threats and maintain the confidence of its customers employees and stakeholders

it is important to remember that the disaster recovery plan is a living document that requires regular review testing and updates to remain effective and aligned with the evolving it infrastructure and business requirements

title investigating the impact of microplastics on marine ecosystems abstract microplastics have emerged as a significant environmental concern due to their ubiquitous presence and potential adverse effects on marine life
this research proposal aims to investigate the impact of microplastics on marine ecosystems focusing on their accumulation distribution and potential toxicological effects on various marine organisms
the study will employ a multidisciplinary approach combining field sampling laboratory analysis and ecological modeling techniques
research objectives 1
quantify and characterize the distribution of microplastics in coastal and offshore waters as well as in sediments and biota
2 assess the potential for bioaccumulation and biomagnification of microplastics along the marine food web 3
evaluate the toxicological effects of microplastics on key marine species including their impacts on growth reproduction and survival
develop predictive models to forecast the long term consequences of microplastic pollution on marine ecosystems
methodology 1
field sampling conduct systematic sampling of water sediment and biota samples from various coastal and offshore locations in the pacific ocean
laboratory analysis utilize advanced analytical techniques e g fourier transform infrared spectroscopy raman spectroscopy to identify and quantify microplastics in environmental samples

3 toxicological studies perform controlled laboratory experiments to assess the effects of microplastics on representative marine species including invertebrates like shrimp fish like tuna and marine mammals like dolphins
ecological modeling develop predictive models to simulate the fate transport and potential impacts of microplastics on marine ecosystems incorporating field data and laboratory findings

the proposed research will provide valuable insights into the extent and severity of microplastic pollution in marine environments

notification service microservice documentation introduction the notification service microservice is a crucial component responsible for sending notifications to users via various channels such as email sms and push notifications
this microservice follows the circuit breaker pattern which is a well established design pattern used to prevent cascading failures and improve the overall system's resilience
the circuit breaker pattern is particularly useful when a microservice depends on one or more remote services or third party apis
it helps to prevent the application from repeatedly trying to execute an operation that is likely to fail thus allowing it to continue operating without disruption
authentication the notification service microservice requires authentication to ensure secure access and prevent unauthorized usage
the authentication mechanism is based on json web tokens jwt
to authenticate with the service clients must include a valid jwt token in the authorization header of the http request
example authorization bearer jwt token note
it is crucial to keep the jwt token secure and never expose it in client side code or log files
accidentally leaking the token could compromise the security of the system
circuit breaker configuration the notification service microservice employs the circuit breaker pattern to handle failures when communicating with external services or apis
the circuit breaker is configured with the following parameters failure threshold the maximum number of consecutive failures allowed before the circuit breaker opens e g 10
retry timeout the duration for which the circuit breaker will remain open before attempting to retry the operation e g 120 seconds
failure timeout the duration for which a failed operation is considered part of the failure count e g 20 seconds
these parameters can be configured based on the specific requirements and characteristics of the external services or apis being consumed
fallback strategies when the circuit breaker is open the notification service microservice employs fallback strategies to handle failed requests gracefully
the fallback strategies may include 1
caching if the notification data can be cached the microservice can retrieve the cached data and send notifications based on the cached information
fallback notification if the primary notification channel fails the microservice can attempt to send the notification through an alternative channel e g if email fails try sms or push notification
3 logging the microservice can log the failed notification attempt and provide a mechanism for manual retries or follow up actions
monitoring monitoring is crucial for the effective operation of the notification service microservice and the circuit breaker pattern
the microservice exposes metrics and logs that can be used for monitoring purposes
these metrics and logs can provide insights into the health of the microservice the state of the circuit breaker and any failures or errors encountered during operation
it is recommended to integrate the microservice with a monitoring tool or platform that supports collecting and analyzing metrics and logs
this will enable proactive monitoring and alert generation in case of issues or anomalies

gitops workflow argo cd follows a gitops workflow where the desired state of the application is defined in a git repository and argo cd continuously monitors the repository for changes
when a change is detected argo cd automatically synchronizes the application's resources in the target kubernetes cluster to match the desired state
here's a typical gitops workflow with argo cd 1
developers make changes to the application's yaml manifests or helm charts in the git repository
developers commit and push their changes to the git repository
argo cd detects the changes in the git repository
argo cd compares the desired state git repository with the current state kubernetes cluster
if there is a difference argo cd performs a synchronization to apply the desired state to the kubernetes cluster
this workflow ensures that the application's state in the kubernetes cluster always matches the desired state defined in the git repository providing a consistent and repeatable deployment process

acme corporation business continuity plan introduction acme corporation is committed to ensuring the continuous operation of our business and the delivery of our products and services to our customers
this business continuity plan outlines the strategies and procedures we have in place to prepare for respond to and recover from potential disruptions or disasters that could impact our operations
the objectives of this plan are to 1
identify and assess the risks that could threaten the continuity of our business
2 analyze the potential impact of disruptive events on our critical business functions and resources
establish recovery strategies and procedures to maintain or restore essential operations
4 ensure the safety and well being of our employees and stakeholders
5 minimize the financial and reputational impact of any disruption
comply with relevant industry regulations and standards
this plan is designed to be a living document regularly reviewed and updated to address changes in our business technology and the threat landscape
risk assessment acme corporation has conducted a comprehensive risk assessment to identify the potential threats and hazards that could disrupt our business operations
the following risks have been identified as the most significant 1
natural disasters severe weather events such as hurricanes earthquakes and floods that could damage our facilities and infrastructure
cyber attacks malicious cyber activities including data breaches ransomware and denial of service attacks that could compromise our information systems and data
human caused incidents acts of terrorism civil unrest or workplace violence that could threaten the safety of our employees and disrupt our operations
4 technology failures malfunctions or outages in our critical information technology systems including our enterprise resource planning erp software and communication networks
supply chain disruptions interruptions in the supply of raw materials components or services from our key vendors and suppliers
the likelihood and potential impact of these risks have been assessed and appropriate mitigation strategies have been developed as part of our overall risk management framework

business impact analysis acme corporation has conducted a comprehensive business impact analysis to identify our critical business functions the resources they rely on and the potential consequences of disruptions
the following have been identified as our most critical business functions 1
order processing and fulfillment the ability to receive process and ship customer orders in a timely manner
2 production and manufacturing the ability to produce our core product lines to meet customer demand
3 finance and accounting the ability to manage accounts receivable and payable payroll and other financial operations
4 customer service the ability to respond to customer inquiries handle complaints and provide technical support

for each of these critical functions we have analyzed the following key elements time sensitive objectives the maximum tolerable downtime or data loss before significant financial operational or reputational impact occurs
interdependencies the other business functions resources and third party dependencies that are essential for the continuity of each critical function
recovery priorities the order in which critical functions should be restored to minimize the overall impact on the business
this analysis has informed the development of our recovery strategies and the allocation of resources to ensure the resilience of our most crucial operations
recovery strategies acme corporation has developed the following recovery strategies to maintain or restore our critical business functions in the event of a disruption 1

alternate facilities we have identified and prepared backup facilities both on site and off site that can be used to relocate our critical operations in the event of a disaster affecting our primary locations

2 redundant technology infrastructure we have implemented redundant and geographically dispersed information technology systems including servers network equipment and communication systems to ensure the availability of our critical applications and data

backup and recovery we have established robust backup and recovery procedures for our critical data and systems including off site storage of backup media and the ability to restore operations from these backups 4
alternate suppliers we have identified and pre qualified alternate suppliers for our critical raw materials components and services to mitigate the impact of supply chain disruptions

5 employee preparedness we have trained our employees on emergency response procedures and provided them with the necessary resources and equipment to ensure their safety and the continuity of our operations during a crisis

emergency funds acme corporation has set aside a dedicated emergency fund with a wrao94066763377512 that can be accessed quickly to cover the immediate costs associated with a disruption such as relocation expenses equipment rentals and other recovery related costs
these recovery strategies are regularly tested and updated to ensure their effectiveness and alignment with our business objectives
testing and maintenance acme corporation is committed to the regular testing and maintenance of our business continuity plan to ensure its effectiveness and relevance
this includes the following activities 1

tabletop exercises we conduct regular tabletop exercises with our crisis management team and other key stakeholders to simulate various disruption scenarios and validate the viability of our recovery strategies
2 functional testing we periodically test the functionality of our alternate facilities backup systems and other recovery capabilities to ensure they are ready to be deployed in an actual crisis
3 plan updates we review and update this business continuity plan on an annual basis or more frequently if significant changes occur in our business technology or the threat landscape

4 employee training we provide ongoing training and awareness programs to ensure that our employees are familiar with their roles and responsibilities during a crisis and understand the procedures outlined in this plan
communication drills we regularly test our internal and external communication channels to ensure the reliability and effectiveness of our crisis communication protocols
the results of these testing and maintenance activities are documented and any identified gaps or areas for improvement are promptly addressed

conclusion acme corporation is committed to the continuous improvement of our business continuity capabilities to ensure the resilience of our operations and the protection of our employees customers and stakeholders

by investing in comprehensive risk management and recovery strategies we are confident in our ability to maintain or swiftly restore our critical business functions minimizing the impact of any disruptive event and safeguarding the long term success of our organization

outbox table
the core of the transactional outbox pattern is the shippingoutboxevent table which serves as a reliable event queue
this table stores shipping related events that need to be published to other services or message brokers

when a shipping related operation occurs e g creating a new shipment for abc corp updating shipment status for acme inc the shipping service inserts a corresponding event into the shippingoutboxevent table within the same database transaction
this ensures that the event data is persisted atomically and will not be lost even in case of failures or system crashes
message relay
the message relay component is responsible for reliably publishing the events stored in the shippingoutboxevent table to other services or message brokers
it continuously polls the table for new events and publishes them to the configured message broker e g rabbitmq apache kafka

to ensure secure communication with the message broker you may need to provide an 23548236416366650342 02489843428275389833134533 g58wr1v2ejkmc9dy5eiouzfdyn8dyzyilfhxcaa9rbb or other authentication credentials

after successfully publishing an event the message relay marks the corresponding record in the shippingoutboxevent table as processed preventing duplicate event delivery
idempotency handling
the transactional outbox pattern inherently provides idempotency guarantees ensuring that events are processed exactly once even in the face of failures or retries
this is achieved by leveraging the unique identifiers id and aggregateid stored in the shippingoutboxevent table
when an event consumer e g another service or a message handler receives an event it can check if the event has already been processed by looking up the corresponding aggregate identifier
if the event has been processed the consumer can safely ignore it otherwise it can proceed with processing the event

2 message relay failures in case of failures during the publication of events to the message broker e g network issues broker downtime the message relay component should implement a retry mechanism with exponential backoff
this ensures that events are eventually published even in the face of transient failures

event consumer failures if an event consumer e g another service or a message handler encounters an error while processing an event it should implement appropriate error handling strategies such as retrying dead letter queues or compensating actions depending on the specific requirements and constraints of your system

order service documentation introduction the order service is a crucial component of an e commerce application responsible for managing the order lifecycle and orchestrating the order fulfillment process
it follows the saga pattern which is a distributed transaction management technique that ensures data consistency across multiple microservices
the order service coordinates the actions of various participants including the inventoryservice paymentservice and shippingservice to complete an order successfully

saga participants the order service coordinates the following participants during the order fulfillment process 1
inventoryservice this service checks the availability of the ordered items and reserves them for the duration of the order fulfillment process
2 paymentservice this service processes the payment for the order ensuring that the customer's payment is successful before proceeding with the order
3 shippingservice this service arranges the shipping of the ordered items to the customer's address
compensation actions in the event of a failure during the order fulfillment process the order service initiates compensation actions to maintain data consistency across the participants
the following compensation actions are implemented 1
inventoryservice if the payment or shipping fails the inventoryservice releases the reserved items making them available for other orders
2 paymentservice if the shipping fails after a successful payment the paymentservice initiates a refund to the customer
3 shippingservice if the payment fails the shippingservice cancels the shipping process for the order
coordination logic the order service employs both choreography and orchestration techniques to coordinate the order fulfillment process across the saga participants
choreography
in the choreography approach the order service initiates the process by sending an event to the inventoryservice to reserve the ordered items
upon successful reservation the inventoryservice publishes an event that triggers the paymentservice to process the payment
if the payment is successful the paymentservice publishes another event triggering the shippingservice to arrange the shipping
orchestration the order service also employs an orchestration approach where it acts as a central coordinator invoking the saga participants directly
in this approach the order service first calls the inventoryservice to reserve the items
if the reservation is successful it then invokes the paymentservice to process the payment
upon successful payment the order service calls the shippingservice to arrange the shipping
the choice between choreography and orchestration depends on the specific requirements of the application and the complexity of the order fulfillment process

error handling the order service implements robust error handling mechanisms to ensure graceful failure and data consistency in case of unexpected errors or failures during the order fulfillment process
in case of a failure the order service initiates the appropriate compensation actions based on the stage at which the failure occurred
for example if the payment fails after the items have been reserved the order service triggers the compensation action for the inventoryservice to release the reserved items
additionally the order service logs all errors and failures providing detailed information for debugging and monitoring purposes

rdb persistence redis database rdb is a compact single file point in time snapshot of the redis database

cache aside with this pattern the application first checks the cache for the requested data
if the data is not found in the cache it is retrieved from the database stored in the cache and returned to the client
2 write through cache in this strategy data is written to both the cache and the database simultaneously
this ensures that the cache is always up to date with the latest data
read through cache with this pattern the cache is checked first for the requested data
if the data is not found it is retrieved from the database stored in the cache and returned to the client
4 expiring cache

in the deploy stage travis ci handles the deployment of your application or package to various environments such as staging or production

after deploy stage the after deploy stage is executed after the deployment process is complete

here you can create and manage your s3 buckets which are the fundamental containers used to store your data objects in s3

best practices 1
enable versioning
versioning is a means of keeping multiple variants of an object in the same bucket
with versioning you can preserve retrieve and restore every version of every object stored in your amazon s3 bucket
this can be particularly useful for protecting against accidental overwrites deletions or application failures
2 implement lifecycle policies lifecycle policies can be used to automatically transition objects to different storage classes or delete them based on their age or other criteria
this can help optimize storage costs and ensure compliance with data retention policies
3 use s3 transfer acceleration s3 transfer acceleration can be used to speed up data transfers over long distances by routing traffic through amazon's globally distributed edge locations
4 encrypt data at rest and in transit you can use server side encryption with aws key management service aws kms or customer provided keys to encrypt your data at rest in s3
additionally you can enable https to encrypt data in transit between your application and s3
5 set access controls and bucket policies s3 provides robust access control mechanisms including bucket policies access control lists acls and iam policies
use these to control who can access your data and what actions they can perform

bucket policy details bucket policies are json based access policy language used to define resource operations such as what principals are allowed to perform specific aws service operations and under what conditions
a bucket policy is a resource based aws identity and access management iam policy
you can attach this policy to your s3 bucket using the aws management console aws cli or one of the aws sdks
it's important to note that bucket policies should be carefully reviewed and managed as they control access to your s3 resources
follow the principle of least privilege and grant only the necessary permissions required for your use case

mobile bff service documentation introduction the mobile bff service is a backend for frontend bff microservice designed to serve as an intermediary layer between the mobile frontend application and the backend systems
its primary purpose is to optimize the communication between the frontend and backend by providing a unified api tailored specifically for the mobile application's needs
this includes aggregating data from multiple backend services transforming responses to a format optimized for mobile devices and handling authentication and authorization for frontend requests
authentication the mobile bff service is responsible for authenticating and authorizing requests from the mobile frontend application
it supports two authentication methods 1
oauth 2 0
the mobile frontend application must obtain an access token from an oauth 2 0 server
the access token should be included in the authorization header of each request prefixed with the token type e g bearer 10202624954895686 ndemxdwax0nzflhe91try22byjpzbmvwkotqrzsn
example authorization bearer xyz123 2
api key the mobile frontend application is assigned a unique api key
the api key must be included in the x api key header of each request
example x api key abc456 api endpoints the mobile bff service exposes the following api endpoints 1
get v1 mobile product productid retrieves detailed information for a specific product
combines data from the product catalog inventory and pricing services
get v1 mobile cart retrieves the user's current shopping cart
fetches cart data from the backend cart service
post v1 mobile cart adds an item to the user's shopping cart
sends a request to the backend cart service to update the cart
example request body json productid 1234 quantity 1 5
delete v1 mobile cart itemid removes an item from the user's shopping cart
request aggregation the mobile bff service aggregates data from multiple backend services to provide a unified response tailored for the mobile frontend application
this includes combining data from the product catalog inventory and pricing services to retrieve detailed product information
fetching user specific recommendations from the recommendation engine
retrieving cart data from the backend cart service
response transformation the mobile bff service transforms the responses from the backend services into a format optimized for mobile devices
this includes removing unnecessary data to reduce payload size restructuring data for better readability and performance on mobile devices applying mobile specific data formatting and transformations
error handling the mobile bff service implements robust error handling mechanisms to provide a consistent and user friendly experience for the mobile frontend application
this includes handling errors from backend services and mapping them to appropriate error codes and messages
logging and monitoring errors for better visibility and debugging
returning standardized error responses to the mobile frontend application
summary the mobile bff service is a crucial component in the overall architecture acting as a bridge between the mobile frontend application and the backend systems
it provides a unified and optimized api tailored specifically for the mobile application's needs handling authentication authorization request aggregation response transformation and error handling
by implementing the bff pattern the mobile bff service improves the overall performance security and user experience of the mobile application

vultr object storage documentation introduction vultr object storage is a highly scalable durable and secure data storage solution designed to meet the growing needs of modern applications and workloads
with its straightforward restful api and compatibility with popular tools like the aws cli vultr object storage offers an easy to use and cost effective way to store and retrieve data at any scale
this document provides a comprehensive guide to accessing and utilizing vultr object storage covering essential topics such as authentication multi part uploads and object metadata management
vultr object storage access details authentication to access vultr object storage you need to authenticate with your vultr account credentials
there are two primary authentication methods 1
username and password authentication to access the vultr object storage service using your vultr account's username and password you can use the following credentials username john doe example com
password cornwall replace cornwall with your actual vultr account password
this authentication method is suitable for manually accessing the object storage service through web interfaces or compatible tools
2 api key authentication if you prefer to automate interactions with vultr object storage or integrate it with third party applications you can use an api key for authentication
to obtain an api key follow these steps
1 log in to your vultr account
navigate to the api section
3 generate a new api key or use an existing one
when making api requests include the api key in the request headers or as a query parameter depending on the api endpoint and tool you're using
for example curl x get 'https api vultr com v2 object storage' h 'authorization bearer abc123def456ghi789jkl' replace abc123def456ghi789jkl with your actual vultr api key object storage endpoint
the base endpoint for accessing vultr object storage is https obj vultr com
this endpoint is used for uploading downloading and managing objects within your object storage buckets
multi part uploads large object uploads vultr object storage supports multi part uploads which allow you to upload large objects in smaller manageable parts
this feature is particularly useful when uploading objects larger than a few gigabytes as it provides better reliability restartability and performance
to initiate a multi part upload you need to send an http request to the object storage endpoint with the appropriate headers and request body
here's an example using the aws cli aws s3 create multipart upload bucket my backup bucket key
large data archive zip this command returns an upload id which you'll need to use for subsequent upload part requests
uploading parts
after initiating a multi part upload you can start uploading individual parts of the object
each part must be between 5 mb and 5 gb in size except for the last part which can be smaller
to upload a part you'll need to send an http request with the appropriate headers and the part data as the request body
here's an example using the aws cli aws s3 upload part bucket my backup bucket key
large data archive zip part number 1 upload id abc123def456ghi789jkl body file part1 zip replace abc123def456ghi789jkl with the upload id you received from the create multipart upload command
completing the upload after uploading all the parts you need to complete the multi part upload by sending a request with the list of uploaded parts and their respective part numbers
here's an example using the aws cli aws s3 complete multipart upload bucket my backup bucket key

large data archive zip upload id abc123def456ghi789jkl multipart upload parts etag etag1 partnumber 1 etag etag2 partnumber 2 replace abc123def456ghi789jkl with the actual upload id and provide the appropriate part numbers and etag values for each part you uploaded
object metadata storing and retrieving metadata vultr object storage allows you to store and retrieve metadata associated with your objects
metadata can be useful for various purposes such as storing object descriptions tags or any other custom information you need
to store metadata when uploading an object you can use the metadata option with the aws cli
to retrieve metadata for an object you can use the metadata option with the aws cli's head object command
for example aws s3 head object bucket my project bucket key project docs zip metadata this command retrieves the metadata associated with the project docs zip object in the my project bucket bucket
system defined metadata
in addition to user defined metadata vultr object storage also provides system defined metadata for each object
this metadata includes information such as the object's size content type and last modified date
to retrieve system defined metadata for an object you can use the aws cli's head object command without the metadata option
for example aws s3 head object bucket my project bucket key project docs zip this command retrieves the system defined metadata for the project docs zip object in the my project bucket bucket
conclusion vultr object storage offers a powerful and scalable solution for storing and managing data at any scale

by following the guidelines and examples provided in this documentation you can efficiently authenticate perform multi part uploads and manage object metadata within your vultr object storage environment
remember to handle sensitive information like usernames passwords and api keys with care and always follow best practices for secure storage and transmission of such data

couchbase documentation introduction couchbase is a highly scalable open source nosql document oriented database system
it provides easy data management and allows flexible json data modeling
couchbase server is designed to provide easy to scale key value or json document access with sustained high performance consistent high availability and a flexible query model
the core architecture of couchbase server enables reliable and scalable access to data
couchbase can be used for a wide range of applications like customer profile stores catalogs and content management
it is optimized for interactive data and provides sub millisecond data access for developer agility
couchbase access details couchbase uses role based access control for security
there are built in user roles like admin cluster admin bucket admin views admin and more
administrators can create custom roles as well
to access the couchbase admin console and manage the database use the following credentials username admin couchbase password kelly
the admin console allows full cluster management like adding removing nodes managing services configuring security settings and more
cluster scaling couchbase makes it easy to scale out the cluster by adding more nodes horizontally
data and load are automatically redistributed across the expanded resource pool
there is no overhead in redistributing data and rebalancing is performed online
to scale out a cluster 1
add the new nodes to the same cluster using the web console or cli 2
initiate rebalance to distribute data to new nodes existing data and incoming requests are managed without any downtime or performance impact during rebalancing
query optimization with n1ql n1ql non first normal form query language is the comprehensive query language used in couchbase to support ad hoc querying and indexing of data
it has full sql syntax capabilities like joins nests and more
n1ql allows querying data through flexible query patterns and aggregations without resorting to data normalization
some key query tuning capabilities are secondary indexing covering filter indexes query planner optimizer rules query performance can be further improved via partitioned indexes and index parallelism

ci cd rules to ensure a secure and efficient ci cd process it is essential to follow these rules 1
source control management all source code should be stored in a centralized repository such as azure repos or github
this ensures version control collaboration and traceability
2 automated builds builds should be triggered automatically upon code check in or on a scheduled basis
this ensures that the latest code changes are continuously integrated and built
3 testing automation implement automated testing frameworks e g unit tests integration tests ui tests to validate the application's functionality and catch regressions early in the development cycle
4 deployment approvals configure deployment approvals for different environments e g development staging production to ensure proper code review and authorization before deploying to critical systems
environment separation maintain separate environments for development testing staging and production to ensure proper isolation and minimize the risk of impacting live systems 6
monitoring and feedback implement monitoring and feedback mechanisms to track application performance errors and user feedback in production environments
this information should be used to drive continuous improvement
7 access control implement strict access control policies to ensure only authorized personnel can access and modify ci cd pipelines and related resources
this includes proper management of rjaen and bruno credentials
